recentEmptyResults.title: 2 · Investigate flow vulnerabilities
recentEmptyResults.explanation: No exploitable bug in the code-less-recipient buyEntries path. Raffle.sol:209-237 takes exactly entryCount*ENTRY_PRICE of USDC from msg.sender before it writes any state. The overflow guard (entryCount <= uint128.max - totalEntries) keeps the entry ranges in bounds, and the uint256 product cannot overflow. Ticket IDs and ranges are contiguous and never reused, so unsettledPot always equals totalEntries*ENTRY_PRICE and the later refund and settlement math stays solvent. Skipping the isRaffle lookup (Raffle.sol:602) and the receiver callback (ERC721Utils.sol:32) for code-less addresses is documented, standard ERC-721 behavior. The lead's scenario is a buyer minting to a CREATE-predicted future clone address or to a contract still in its constructor. That only lets the buyer strand their own paid ticket, the same as minting to any keyless address such as 0x...dEaD, which no ERC-721 screen can stop. A stranded ticket has no effect on anyone else. Other holders' win odds and refund amounts are unchanged, sponsor and treasury allocations are unchanged, and settlement stays permissionless. The ticket is inert inside a clone: Raffle has no arbitrary-call path, and RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams rejects registered raffles as prize tokens. An attacker cannot force a victim's chosen recipient to become a clone address, because that would require a CREATE address collision. A clone also has no window where it holds code but is unregistered and makes untrusted calls: its initcode makes no calls, initialize calls only the trusted factory, and the factory sets isRaffle before the untrusted prize transfer. So there is no attacker-to-victim impact here.

recentEmptyResults.title: 2 · Investigate flow vulnerabilities
recentEmptyResults.explanation:
I found no supported vulnerability in the input-validation rejection path of Raffle.buyEntries (packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:209-221).

1. All three guards run before any external call or state write. The zero-recipient check is at L217, the entryCount == 0 check at L218 and the overflow check at L219-221. If any of them reverts, the safeTransferFrom at L224 never runs, so no funds move and no state changes.

2. The overflow check is correct. `type(uint128).max - totalEntries` cannot underflow because totalEntries is a uint128. So any accepted entryCount gives `totalEntries + entryCount <= 2^128-1`. Together with entryCount >= 1, that guarantees `1 <= firstEntry <= lastEntry` and contiguous ranges that do not overlap. Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic would also catch any wrap.

3. The downstream math stays in bounds:
   - grossAmount is at most about 2^148 in uint256.
   - A full 100-ticket refund batch is at most about 2^155.
   - The refund width at L363 is exactly entryCount for any minted ticket. Unminted or burned IDs revert at ownerOf first.
   - The winner modulo at L518 gives a value in [1, totalEntries] that fits in uint128. requestDraw already enforces totalEntries > 0, and the Drawing status blocks any later purchase.
   - The range check at L579-585 rejects ticket ID 0 and unminted IDs, whose stored range is (0,0), because winningEntry is always >= 1.

4. Purchases and draws cannot overlap. buyEntries requires `block.timestamp < endTime`, while requestDraw requires `block.timestamp >= endTime` and moves the status off Active. A buyer can never buy after the randomness is known.

5. Screening recipients against protocol addresses inside _update (after payment) is safe. A rejected recipient reverts the whole transaction, including the USDC pull. Any address that passes the screen but cannot use the ticket only loses the buyer's own funds. Settlement and the sponsor and treasury claims do not depend on who owns the winning ticket.

6. The lack of a per-buyer cap is intended, and it is not profitable to exploit:
   - If the reserve is missed, the winner gets back at most 80% of the gross.
   - If the reserve is met, the sponsor gets 95% of at least the reserve price, which is the price the sponsor chose to accept.
   - Pushing totalEntries toward the uint128 limit to block other buyers would cost about 3.4e38 USDC, which is impossible.

Clones share the immutable values factory, quoteToken and i_vrfV2PlusWrapper. The reentrancy guard works on uninitialized clone storage, the implementation is locked in Refunding status, and Active can only be reached through the factory's atomic prize deposit.

recentEmptyResults.title: 2 · Investigate flow vulnerabilities
recentEmptyResults.explanation: No exploitable bug found in the buyEntries status and time gate. Every non-Active state reverts at Raffle.sol:215, and the time check at :216 cannot be bypassed. (1) Lifecycle: status is written in only six places (L165, 205, 252, 299, 428, 521), and status only moves forward. Only initialize sets AwaitingPrize; it is factory-only, runs once, and is guarded by `initialized`. Only onERC721Received sets Active, and it requires AwaitingPrize, msg.sender == prizeToken, the exact tokenId, from == sponsor and operator == factory. requestDraw, enableRefunds and fulfillRandomWords leave Active, and nothing ever sets Active again. The implementation is locked at status=Refunding with initialized=true. Clones made outside the factory can never be initialized (OnlyFactory) and can never become Active, because their prizeToken stays address(0). (2) Time: endTime is set once in initialize. Sales revert when block.timestamp >= endTime, and requestDraw reverts when block.timestamp < endTime, so the two windows never overlap. totalEntries changes only inside buyEntries, so once a draw is requested the entry count and pot are fixed. The VRF modulus and reserve test at L518-521 therefore cannot change after the request. (3) Transient Active window: during RaffleFactory.createRaffle, only the prize contract's own code runs in the same transaction, so only it can buy entries before escrow is verified. That purchase is paid by msg.sender and is fully undone if the checks at RaffleFactory.sol:129-134 revert. Otherwise it is the same as buying in the next block, and position in the entry range gives no advantage. A prize contract that lies about holding the NFT is a fake-prize trust issue, not a bypass of this gate. (4) The OpenZeppelin 5.6.1 reentrancy guard keeps its flag in a dedicated storage slot. In a clone that slot starts at 0, which the guard does not treat as entered, so nonReentrant works on clones. The flag goes back to its prior value on revert.

recentEmptyResults.title: 2 · Investigate flow vulnerabilities
recentEmptyResults.explanation: No exploitable vulnerability exists in this flow. reserveEntries and sponsorRecipient come only from the sponsor's own createRaffle call. Both are checked at creation (RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams and Raffle.initialize: reserve must be nonzero; the recipient cannot be zero, the factory, USDC, the VRF wrapper, the prize token, the implementation, the new clone itself, or any registered raffle), and neither can be changed afterwards. At Raffle.sol:521, totalEntries is already fixed when it is compared to the reserve: buyEntries needs Active status and block.timestamp < endTime, while requestDraw needs block.timestamp >= endTime and moves the raffle to Drawing. Settlement in _settleWinningTicket works on whole multiples of 1e6, so 5%/95% and 5%/80%/15% split exactly and nothing is lost or left unallocated. releaseSponsorProceeds sets sponsorProceeds to zero before paying, and it does not depend on the winner or treasury claims. The payout-time _isProtocolDestination check can only reject sponsorRecipient if the sponsor chose a factory CREATE address that has not been deployed yet, meaning a future clone. Clones are deployed only at the factory's sequential nonce addresses. No third party can turn an existing EOA or contract into a registered raffle, and nobody can obtain the key for one of those addresses. So proceeds become unclaimable only through the sponsor's own mistake, and only the sponsor's share is affected. The sponsor can buy entries to push sales past the reserve, but that is an economic property buyers can see on-chain and that on-chain code cannot prevent. It is not a code-level flaw.

recentEmptyResults.title: 2 · Investigate flow vulnerabilities
recentEmptyResults.explanation: No concrete, third-party-exploitable bug was found in the later prize-release paths. (1) In the NftWon branch of redeemWinningTicket (Raffle.sol:329-337), the stored prizeToken does decide whether delivery succeeds. A failed delivery reverts the burn and every state change, so the winner keeps a transferable ticket and can move it to another address if a recipient-specific restriction applies. A malicious prize contract that blocks or lies gives the sponsor nothing beyond what an honest but worthless NFT already gives. The sponsor still collects 95% through releaseSponsorProceeds, which the spec says is claimable independently of delivery, and the 'prize' is only worth what its own contract allows. The only profitable variant would require the sponsor to hold admin or force-transfer power over a valuable collection, which is a trust assumption about the collection (IRaffle documents supported prizes as honest ERC-721s), not a protocol flaw. (2) The prize contract cannot hurt other parties or other clones. Every state-changing raffle function is nonReentrant. The winning ticket is burned before the external call. _update forbids the prize token as a ticket recipient. The CashWon payout, refunds and fee/proceeds releases never call the prize token. _transferQuote re-screens destinations at payout time. The factory's approvals cannot be abused because from is always msg.sender. (3) releaseSponsorPrize (Raffle.sol:402-405) does not re-screen sponsorRecipient, but the static protocol destinations are immutable and were already checked at creation. The only destination that can appear later is a newly created clone at a predictable future CREATE address. Using one would require the sponsor to deliberately pick that address, which harms only the sponsor's own NFT. A re-check would leave the NFT stuck in the original clone with the same loss, and no third party is affected.
